message:
=== USER DASHBOARD (Admin Panel)

DATA:
- Source: GET /api/users
- Shape: { id, name, email, status: "active"|"inactive"|"pending", created_at, visits }
- Volume: 50–500 rows, fresh from backend each load (no real-time needed yet)
- Performance target: API <1s typical, page interactive <2s

REQUIREMENTS (priority order):

1. CORE TABLE (must have)
   - Paginated: 20 rows/page
   - Columns: name | email | status | created_at | visits
   - Sortable by clicking headers (ascending/descending toggle)
   - Mobile responsive: stack filters vertically, hide "visits" column on small screens
   
2. FILTERS (don't reset pagination, but do reset to page 1 when filters change)
   - Status: multiselect (active, inactive, pending) OR (all) — default to ALL
   - Created date: start date + end date (optional, both inclusive)
   - Search: by name substring (case-insensitive)
   
3. NICE-TO-HAVE (but don't force it)
   - Pie chart showing status distribution
   - CSV export button

CONSTRAINTS:
- Stack: React 18, Tailwind CSS, date-fns (dates only), chart.js + react-chartjs-2 (optional)
- No real-time updates (defer for next sprint)
- No heatmaps, predictions, or complex analytics (defer)
- Error handling required: show user-friendly error if API fails or times out
- Loading state: show skeleton loaders in table while fetching

SUCCESS CRITERIA (measurable):
- Lighthouse Performance ≥85 on simulated slow 4G (DevTools throttling)
- LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) <1.8s
- CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) <0.1
- All filters work without breaking pagination or sorting
- Mobile view tested at 375px width
- Edge case: empty results, API error (403/5xx), slow network (>3s) all handled gracefully

NOTES:
- Backend is stable, no auth issues
- I'll test locally before deploy
- Quality > speed, no urgency
- After this works, I might want to extract date filter logic to a hook for reuse on other pages

Can you build this as a single focused component (UserDashboard.tsx) with clear props/exports so it's testable and easy to refactor later?

Perfect. Just a few small polish questions before we ship:

1. Sorting UI: The bold header works, but it's subtle. Can we add a visual indicator like an underline when it's the sort field? Done is fine if not.

2. Status colors: Can we extract those to a constants file (statusConfig.ts) so they're reusable if we add a status filter component later?

3. CSV: The export includes filtered data (good!), but should we show a toast notification when it completes? Or just let the download happen silently?

4. Lighthouse: I'll run it once locally before deploy. What should I specifically look for? Any quick wins if we're under 85?

5. Date filter: After this ships, I want to extract the date range logic into a custom hook (useDateFilter) for reuse. Would the current structure make that easy?

That's it. This is looking really solid.
